profiles.notes: Reference machine. AcerGamingFunction is registered as a dynamic class; instance access needs elevation. Sensor ids measured against the Acer service at the same moment: GetGamingSysInfo(0x0101)=63 C, (0x0201)=2436 RPM, (0x0301)=55 C, (0x0601)=2409 RPM, (0x0A01)=57 C, matching CPU_TEMPERATURE 63, CPU_FANSPEED 2444, SYS1_TEMPERATURE 55, GPU1_FANSPEED 2422 and GPU1_TEMPERATURE 57. Keyboard colour is written through SetGamingRgbKb with a non-zero zone mask; SetGamingKBBacklight rejects every payload tried.
Same platform family as the AN16-41 with a larger chassis. The sensor ids are the firmware-wide enum, not a measurement on this model; a sensor that answers a non-zero status is discarded at runtime.
Single-zone or four-zone RGB depending on the SKU; the keyboard capability answer decides, not this file. Sensor ids are the firmware-wide enum and are not measured on this model.
Aspire-derived board. WMI fan and mode control is present; the MUX switch is not. Sensor ids are the firmware-wide enum and are not measured on this model.
Nitro V chassis with a 16-inch panel. Sensor ids are the firmware-wide enum and are not measured on this model.

Keyboard is driven over USB HID on this model: the WMI RGB methods answer success and change nothing, so the lighting path falls through to the Acer service or OpenRGB. Sensor ids are the firmware-wide enum and are not measured on this model.
Predator fan ceilings are higher than the Nitro line; the plausibility bound has to allow for it. Sensor ids are the firmware-wide enum and are not measured on this model.

Fallback for any Acer machine the table does not name. Deliberately permissive: a wrong ceiling only widens the plausibility bound, it never enables a feature. The sensor ids are the firmware-wide enum, and every reading is gated on the status byte, so a machine that does not answer the call reports no temperature instead of a wrong one.
